`person:group-essel-zee` · flag: **poor** · confidence: verified · tickers: ZEEL, DISHTV, ZEEMEDIA, SITINET

Flag: POOR. Zee Entertainment (ZEEL) is a good franchise run for the benefit of a levered promoter group. Promoter Essel borrowed against Zee shares for infrastructure/power ventures; pledges rose to ~90% of promoter holding, invocations from Jan-2019 cut the promoter stake from ~42% to ~4%. Regulator findings: SEBI's interim order (Jun-2023) found Chandra and Goenka 'misused their position' to siphon ZEEL funds for associate entities via a sham 'adjustment' of Yes Bank FD-backed letters of comfort; barred them from board posts; SAT set aside the Goenka restriction (Oct-2023) while SEBI's probe continued. Invesco's 2021 requisition to remove Goenka and the collapsed Sony merger (Jan-2024) compounded value loss. New finding: SEBI order of 31-Jul-2026 held ZEEL's Hyderabad land was mortgaged as security for loans to four Essel entities without board/shareholder authorisation; barred ZEEL for two months and Chandra/Goenka for 12 months, with fines (ZEEL Rs 30 lakh, Goenka Rs 58 lakh, Chandra Rs 60 lakh); stock fell ~13%; SAT reserved interim-relief orders and partially relaxed ZEEL's restriction to allow a ~Rs 3,000 cr+ fundraise. Dish TV, Zee Media and Siti have had their own board fights, defaults and lender control. Lesson: a low promoter stake does not end promoter extraction while the family controls management; listed-company assets used as collateral for group debt is a severe signal.

- **regulator findings:** SEBI 2023 interim (fund diversion via LoCs); SEBI 31-Jul-2026 (unauthorised land mortgage)
- **red flags:** pledges ~90%; letters of comfort; listed assets securing promoter debt

- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:US-WMT:fy27-adj-eps-at-or-above-2-89`
- **Method:** promise-tracker credibility · **P(ours)** 0.58 · **P(base)** 0.35 · resolve by 2027-03-01
- **Evidence:** Q3 FY27 earnings presentation (19-Nov-2026): FY27 adjusted EPS guide raised for the third time — $2.75–2.85 (Feb) → $2.80–2.87 (Aug) → $2.84–2.89 (Nov); net sales cc +4.9–5.2%; adjusted operating income cc +8.0–8.6%. Q3 adj EPS $0.65 (+4.8%); FY26 adjusted EPS base $2.64 (which, from memory, was above the top of its own final FY26 range of $2.58–2.63).
- **Why our number differs from base:** Walmart has a recent habit of finishing at or above the top of its final guide, and has raised three times this year; holiday trends and tariff-refund noise are the risks.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** S&P 500 companies finish at or above the top of their final-quarter annual EPS range ~35% of the time.
- **Resolution rule:** YES if Walmart's reported FY27 adjusted EPS (Q4 FY27 earnings release) ≥ $2.89.
- **Resolution source:** Walmart Q4 FY27 earnings 8-K (SEC EDGAR, CIK 104169)
- **Sources used:** https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/104169/000010416926000168/earningspresentationfy27.htm

body:
PEAD v2 (pre-registered; 1,555 cos, 4,272 fresh events, 79% consolidated EPS): bottom SUE quintile −2.73% vs
size-matched controls at 63d (t −3.6, CI excludes 0) — confirmed in two independent periods; quintile 2 equally
weak. Long-only top quintile +2.41% gross / +1.41% net (CI touches 0) — not proven, again. "Positive
announcement-day reaction" filter did not replicate; v1's "mid-cap strongest" reversed (noise).
**Rule (stage 2/3):** treat the bottom two earnings-surprise quintiles as an avoid/exit flag for at least
63 trading days. Don't treat a positive surprise alone as a buy reason. Exploratory subgroups don't survive
fresh data — only pre-registered results count. Live tracker logs from Q3 FY27; verdict after 4 live quarters.

**Signals (stage 3) for lenders:** PEAD on reported EPS mixes treasury gains and provision buffers — before acting on
a quintile 1–2 flag, recompute SUE on (PPOP − normal credit cost) per share. Promise tracker: pass website transcripts
with `--local` (banks often file only a cover letter on NSE); build the KPI CSV with `bank_kpis.py` (+ `--manual` deck
KPIs: NIM, CASA, credit cost, CoD, PCR, slippage); report credibility only against a bank peer median (L18) and add a
guidance-bias column (actual − guide midpoint, bps).

**NBFC differences (to test on the next lender run):** no CASA, so the liability unit is the borrowing mix (bank
lines, NCDs, CP, securitisation, ECB) and its ALM; leverage limits and RBI scale-based regulation layer; co-lending
and DLG/FLDG arrangements as off-balance-sheet risk; collection staff per ₹ cr of book as the physical cost driver.
